text:
Alex P: quick hit  Were finalizing Private onboarding. Whats the absolute-minimum GCP IAM for the runtime SA that will call Cloud KMS to unwrap DEKs (envelope keys)?

Maria G: minimum is tiny: grant roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter on the specific CryptoKey only. Optionally roles/logging.logWriter if the SA sends logs. No admin perms.

Sara K: pattern we recommend in docs: bind decrypt to the single cryptoKey. if you need metadata reads, grant roles/cloudkms.viewer at the keyRing level but prefer to avoid.

Liam T: important: avoid long-lived key files for the runtime. use Workload Identity or short-lived impersonation tokens. reduces blast radius.

Jordan (oncall): some customers want keyrings in a central security project and runtime in customer projects. how do we safely do cross-project decrypt?

Maria G: safe cross-project strategy: create keyRing+cryptoKey in security project. Add an IAM binding for the runtime SA principal on the single cryptoKey resource (roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter). do not grant project-level roles. Example:
```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/security-proj/locations/global/keyRings/customer-ring/cryptoKeys/app-envelope-key \
  --member="serviceAccount:runtime-sa@customer-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter"
```
Run the command from a context that can modify the security project.

Sara K: if you can, use IAM Conditions to tighten usage. Example condition sketch (adjust claims for your setup):
```
condition:
  title: "runtime-sa-only"
  expression: "request.auth.principal == 'serviceAccount:runtime-sa@customer-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com'"
```
(Condition language varies; test in a non-prod tenant.)

Alex P: rotation concerns: customers worry about downtime when rotating KEKs. whats our non-disruptive flow?

Liam T: non-destructive rotation flow we follow: create new keyVersion on same CryptoKey and set it primary. old versions remain usable for decrypt so no immediate re-encrypt required. then run background rewrap to gradually convert stored envelopes.

Sara K: short runbook:
1) create new version:
```
gcloud kms keys versions create --location=global --keyring=customer-ring --key=app-envelope-key
```
2) set primary:
```
gcloud kms keys versions set-primary --location=global --keyring=customer-ring --key=app-envelope-key --version=5
```
3) canary: deploy a small worker that rewraps and validates correctness
4) rollout rewrap job with idempotent checkpoints

Maria G: rewrap note: envelopes are typically DEK-wrapped. Rewrap steps: decrypt wrapped DEK with old KEK, encrypt DEK with new KEK, write back. Keep old keyVersions until rewrap completes and verification passes.

Jordan (oncall): monitoring/alerts we should add for rotation and incidents?

Liam T: we monitor: decrypt error rate (from Cloud Audit logs), decrypt latency P95, and number of KMS AccessDenied events. example thresholds: alert if decrypt errors >0.5% sustained for 10m or P95 latency >200ms above baseline for 5m. export audit logs to BigQuery/PubSub for richer analysis.

Sara K: sample audit filter for a sink (Encrypt/Decrypt events):
```
logName="projects/SEC_PROJ/logs/cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Factivity" AND protoPayload.serviceName="cloudkms.googleapis.com" AND (protoPayload.methodName:"Encrypt" OR protoPayload.methodName:"Decrypt")
```
Send to Pub/Sub for lightweight processing (rate counts) and to BigQuery for forensic queries.

Alex P: incident path: if runtime SA credentials leaked, whats immediate containment?

Maria G: fast incident checklist (containment):
- remove the SAs decrypt binding on the cryptoKey immediately:
```
gcloud kms keys remove-iam-policy-binding projects/security-proj/locations/global/keyRings/customer-ring/cryptoKeys/app-envelope-key \
  --member="serviceAccount:runtime-sa@customer-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com" --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter"
```
- create/activate new keyVersion and set primary so future envelopes use new KEK
- start rewrap job for stored data (read old envelopes, decrypt with old keyVersion, encrypt DEK with new primary)
- snapshot and export Cloud Audit logs for the compromise window to a secure bucket
- disable runtime paths that might still use leaked creds (impersonation bindings, external tokens)
- notify security/custodian teams per incident policy

Sara K: nuance: if SA only had decrypt bindings, immediate removal prevents new decrypt operations. but if KEK material itself was exfiltrated, rewrap is required because decryption may already be possible offline.

Liam T: operational tip: implement short-lived KEK use checks in code: prefer calling KMS decrypt at runtime for DEK unwrap and avoid caching long-term decrypted DEKs in process memory or persistent stores where possible.

Jordan (oncall): can we include a simple pseudocode rewrap snippet in the docs?

Alex P: yes, include this minimal pattern:
```
for envelope in storage_batch:
  old_wrapped = envelope.kek_wrapped_key
  dek = KMS.decrypt(old_wrapped)
  plaintext_blob = decrypt_with_DEK(dek, envelope.ciphertext)
  new_wrapped = KMS.encrypt(new_primary_resource, dek)
  write_back(envelope.id, new_wrapped, ciphertext=plaintext_blob)  # idempotent write
  mark_checkpoint(envelope.id)
```
Parallelize, checkpoint by ID ranges, include retry/backoff. After job completes, verify checksums and then destroy old keyVersions if policy allows.

Maria G: include IAM snippet in onboarding: minimal bindings + optional viewer:
```
bindings:
- role: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
  members:
  - serviceAccount:runtime-sa@customer-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
- role: roles/logging.logWriter
  members:
  - serviceAccount:runtime-sa@customer-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
Apply the decrypt role narrowly to the cryptoKey resource.

Sara K: also document cloud region tradeoffs: use regional keyRings for strict residency, global if latency/resilience across regions is desired. keep runtime co-located with key region to reduce egress and latency.

Liam T: and finally: for multi-cloud customers, map equivalents: AWS kms:Decrypt on CMK, Azure KeyVault unwrapKey/unwrapKey permissions. Keep the same minimal-principle approach.
